summary.text: In the traditional analysis, 妹 combines 女, marking a female-person category, with 未 as a sound element. Its common meaning is “younger sister”; disputed early readings do not establish that analysis for every oracle-bone use.

formation.text: The traditional dictionary analysis treats 妹 as a phonosemantic compound: 女 contributes a female-person category and 未 supplies a sound cue. The analysis is also applied to early forms, though readings of some oracle-bone uses are disputed.

components.text: 女 contributes the female-person category in the traditional analysis of 妹. The cited evidence does not specify a distinct earlier form or graphic change.
未 is identified as the phonetic component in the traditional analysis. The reconstructions show historical comparisons with 妹, but are not direct records of ancient speech.

sound_limitation.text: These reconstructions support a comparison, but do not independently establish the identity or role of this component in every early use of 妹.

sound.text: The Zhengzhang Old Chinese reconstructions are similar, with a difference in vowel length notation.
In the separate Baxter–Sagart system, the reconstructions provide a historical comparison; they should not be merged with Zhengzhang forms.
In Modern Mandarin, 未 and 妹 are read wèi and mèi respectively; this modern resemblance alone does not prove their ancient phonetic relationship.

history.text: The dossier documents 妹 forms in oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and clerical scripts. These labels identify forms from different periods but do not by themselves establish a continuous sequence of graphic changes.
The traditional analysis identifies 未 as the sound element. An older explanation associated 妹 with 末, but the evidence here does not show that 未 arose through graphic corruption of 末.

uncertainties.text: Some oracle-bone uses and the bronze phrase 女妹辰 have been interpreted as referring to 昧, “before daybreak.” Other proposals include a place name or a negative word; the bronze phrase has also been read as referring to childhood. These readings do not establish a semantic path to “younger sister.”

Reconstructions support a historical sound comparison between 未 and 妹, but ancient pronunciation is reconstructed rather than directly recorded. Modern Mandarin readings alone do not prove the ancient relationship.
Comparative proposals linking 妹 to other language families are listed, but their evidence is not assessed in this dossier.

senses.period: attested in bronze inscriptions; exact date of the cited example unresolved
senses.text: A bronze inscription is read with the kinship sense “younger sister,” also given in the historical gloss 女弟. This does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning.

senses.period: oracle-bone and bronze inscription readings; phrase interpretation disputed
senses.text: Some early forms and a bronze phrase are interpreted as 妹 used to write 昧, “before daybreak” or “dawn twilight.” If this is borrowing, the graph was reused for a different word because the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation and its relation to the kinship word are not established.

senses.gloss: younger female relative of the same generation
senses.text: Historical dictionary examples attest 妹 for a younger female relative of the same generation. The evidence does not date this sense or derive it from “younger sister.”
A broader use meaning “young woman” is attested, but its chronology and relation to the kinship sense are not established.

senses.gloss: modest first-person reference by a woman
senses.period: later literary use; exact dating unresolved
senses.text: Historical examples attest 妹 as a woman’s modest first-person reference. The evidence does not establish when or how this usage developed.

limitations.text: The early readings do not establish whether the dawn-related use belonged to the same spoken word as the kinship sense or whether the graph was reused for a different word. If it was reused, the proposed mechanism is that the words sounded alike or similar; the old word’s pronunciation is not established here.
The broader and literary senses are attested, but the available examples do not establish their chronology or paths of development.

overview.text: In the traditional analysis, 妹 combines 女, marking a female-person category, with 未 as a sound element. Its common meaning is “younger sister”; disputed oracle-bone readings leave that early use unsettled.

components.text: In the traditional analysis, 女 marks the female-person category in 妹.
The traditional analysis identifies 未 as the sound element; ancient readings are reconstructed, not directly recorded.

relationships.text: The traditional 女 + 未 analysis assigns 女 the female-person category in 妹; readings of some early uses remain disputed.

The traditional analysis identifies 未 as the phonetic element. Zhengzhang compares 未 *mɯds with 妹 *mɯːds; Baxter–Sagart separately compares 未 *m[ə]t-s with 妹 *C.mˤə[t]-s. These reconstructions are not direct records of ancient speech, and the modern Mandarin pair wèi/mèi does not independently establish the ancient role.
